papers.title: WIP: A Pedagogical Prompt Engineering Framework for LLM-Based Feedback in Higher Education (PPE-LLM)
papers.abstract: This Work-in-Progress (WIP) paper introduces PPE-LLM, a structured framework for prompt engineering that enables LLM -generated feedback to be pedagogically meaningful and tailored to novice programming students in introductory pro-gramming education. Although large language models (LLMs) show promise for feedback generation, existing research lacks a structured methodology that integrates pedagogical principles, student needs, best-practice prompting, and technical consid-erations. PPE- LLM addresses this gap by providing a theory-driven framework that supports the systematic design of prompts to generate formative feedback, enhancing learning tailored to students' learning levels and needs. This paper presents the key components of the framework, along with a practical example prompt. It also analyses the alignment of recent CER studies with the PPE- LLM components. The results indicate that studies with limited alignment often produced inconsistent or lower-quality feedback, whereas more substantial alignment was found to be pedagogically effective in AI-generated feedback. Future work includes expert validation and student evaluation in real-world settings.

papers.title: Enhancing High School Programming Education Through LLM-Based Hint Generation
papers.abstract: The integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) into education offers new opportunities for enhancing programming instruction, especially at the high school level. This paper introduces PythonTutor, an intelligent tutoring system that supports novice learners through scaffolded, AI-generated feedback. Powered by ChatGPT 4.0 Mini, PythonTutor provides step-by-step hints tailored to student submissions, promoting independent problem-solving and limiting overreliance on AI. The platform unifies instructional content, personalized tutoring, and teacher oversight in a web-based environment. A pilot study with 18 students and three teachers compared PythonTutor-supported instruction to traditional methods. Results showed significantly greater learning gains with PythonTutor, supported by high accuracy and precision in AI feedback. Student and teacher feedback confirmed the system’s usability, educational value, and classroom potential. PythonTutor emerges as a scalable, cost-effective solution for personalized programming education aligned with best practices

papers.title: Cinema, Fermi Problems, & General Education
papers.abstract: During the past several years the authors have developed a new approach to the teaching of Physical Science, a general education course typically found in the curricula of nearly every college and university. This approach, called `Physics in Films', uses scenes from popular movies to illustrate physical principles and has excited student interest and improved student performance. The analyses of many of the scenes in `Physics in Films' are a direct application of Fermi calculations -- estimates and approximations designed to make solutions of complex and seemingly intractable problems understandable to the student non-specialist. The intent of this paper is to provide instructors with examples they can use to develop skill in recognizing Fermi problems and making Fermi calculations in their own courses.

papers.title: Twelve Years of Education and Public Outreach with the Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope
papers.abstract: During the past twelve years, NASA's Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope has supported a wide range of Education and Public Outreach (E/PO) activities, targeting K-14 students and the general public. The purpose of the Fermi E/PO program is to increase student and public understanding of the science of the high-energy Universe, through inspiring, engaging and educational activities linked to the mission's science objectives. The E/PO program has additional more general goals, including increasing the diversity of students in the Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) pipeline, and increasing public awareness and understanding of Fermi science and technology. Fermi's multi-faceted E/PO program includes elements in each major outcome category: Higher Education; Elementary and Secondary Education; Informal Education and Public Outreach.

summary: The literature on LLM-based feedback generation for programming education highlights the integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) to provide tailored feedback, particularly through frameworks like PPE-LLM and systems such as PythonTutor. These studies indicate significant learning gains compared to traditional methods, yet they face limitations in empirical validation and expert evaluation. There is a notable gap in systematically applying pedagogical principles to LLM feedback mechanisms, suggesting a need for further exploration and real-world assessments.
scholarly_positioning: While prior approaches, such as the PPE-LLM framework and PythonTutor system, demonstrate the potential of LLMs to enhance programming education through tailored feedback, they are hindered by a lack of comprehensive empirical validation and expert evaluation across diverse educational contexts. Existing studies primarily focus on isolated implementations without a systematic application of pedagogical principles, leaving unresolved tensions regarding the effectiveness and scalability of these solutions. Furthermore, the limited sample sizes and preliminary nature of findings underscore the insufficiency of current work in establishing robust, generalizable frameworks for LLM-based feedback. This proposed research aims to address these gaps by rigorously validating LLM feedback mechanisms in real-world settings, thereby contributing to a broader discourse on the integration of AI in educational practices.
research_scope: This study will empirically validate the effectiveness of the PPE-LLM framework and the PythonTutor system in enhancing programming education among high school students learning Python. The evaluation period will span one academic semester, during which students will receive LLM-generated feedback on their coding assignments. A control group will utilize traditional feedback methods, allowing for a comparative analysis of learning outcomes. Primary outcomes will include improvements in coding proficiency measured through pre- and post-tests, while secondary outcomes will assess student engagement and satisfaction through qualitative surveys. The study aims to provide robust evidence for the scalability and pedagogical alignment of LLM-based feedback mechanisms in diverse educational settings.

technical_feasibility: The study requires access to open-source LLMs for interpretability analysis and hidden state extraction, as well as human participants for qualitative surveys and user trust assessments, necessitating ethics approval. It also requires GPU resources for model deployment and testing. Additionally, labeled datasets for training and evaluation may be needed, along with annotation protocols for qualitative feedback analysis. A feasible adjustment would be to utilize an existing API model for initial evaluations while focusing on output-level explanations, thereby reducing the need for hidden-state access.
gap: Prior studies have demonstrated the potential of LLMs to enhance programming education through tailored feedback in contexts such as high school settings; however, they treat the empirical validation of these frameworks as secondary, leaving unclear whether the pedagogical alignment of LLM-generated feedback affects learning outcomes and student engagement; this matters practically because effective feedback mechanisms are crucial for improving student performance in programming; therefore, this study investigates the effectiveness of the PPE-LLM framework and PythonTutor system in real-world educational settings over an academic semester.
question: How does the implementation of the PPE-LLM framework and PythonTutor system, compared to traditional feedback methods, affect coding proficiency and student engagement among high school students learning Python over one academic semester?
theoretical_mechanism: The independent variable is the type of feedback method (LLM-based vs. traditional). The mediator is the pedagogical alignment of the feedback provided, which influences the learning outcomes. The moderator is the level of student engagement, which may affect how feedback is received and utilized. The dependent variables are coding proficiency and student engagement. The theoretical framework is grounded in constructivist learning theories, suggesting that personalized feedback enhances learning through active engagement. The causal chain posits that LLM-generated feedback, when pedagogically aligned, improves coding proficiency by fostering deeper understanding, while higher engagement levels further amplify this effect. Assumptions requiring empirical validation include the effectiveness of LLM feedback in diverse educational contexts and the impact of engagement on learning outcomes.
hypothesis: High school students receiving LLM-generated feedback through the PPE-LLM framework will demonstrate greater improvements in coding proficiency compared to those receiving traditional feedback methods, with the effect being mediated by the pedagogical alignment of the feedback.

methodology: This study will employ a controlled experimental design involving two groups of high school students learning Python: one receiving LLM-generated feedback through the PPE-LLM framework and the other receiving traditional feedback methods. Participants will be assessed using pre- and post-tests to measure coding proficiency, while qualitative surveys will gauge student engagement and satisfaction. The pedagogical alignment of the feedback will be evaluated mid-semester through expert assessments. Statistical analyses will compare learning outcomes between groups, controlling for potential confounds such as prior knowledge and motivation. The study aims to ensure reproducibility by following a structured protocol for feedback delivery and assessment, while the scope will be limited to one academic semester to maintain focus and feasibility.

proposal: This research proposal aims to empirically validate the effectiveness of LLM-based feedback mechanisms, specifically the PPE-LLM framework and the PythonTutor system, in enhancing programming education for high school students learning Python through structured coding assignments over one academic semester. Key concepts such as LLM (Large Language Model), pedagogical alignment, and coding proficiency will be operationally defined to ensure clarity. The motivation for this study stems from the significant learning gains reported in existing literature, yet there remains a critical gap in empirical validation and pedagogical integration of LLM-generated feedback, particularly in diverse educational contexts. The central research question investigates how LLM-generated feedback compares to traditional methods in terms of coding proficiency and student engagement. The theoretical mechanism posits that the type of feedback influences pedagogical alignment (mediator), which in turn affects learning outcomes (dependent variable), moderated by student engagement (moderator). The falsifiable hypothesis states that students receiving LLM-generated feedback will show greater improvements in coding proficiency than those receiving traditional feedback methods, with pedagogical alignment mediating this effect. Constructs will be operationalized using pre- and post-tests for coding proficiency, qualitative surveys for student engagement, and expert evaluations for pedagogical alignment. A controlled experimental design will ensure comparability between groups, with traditional feedback serving as a baseline. The study will employ valid metrics and statistical controls to address potential confounds such as prior knowledge and motivation, ensuring robust empirical evidence. The expected contributions include theoretical advancements in understanding LLM feedback mechanisms, technical validation of the PPE-LLM framework, empirical evidence of its effectiveness, and practical guidelines for educators. Key limitations may include variability in student prior knowledge and engagement levels, which will be addressed through stratified sampling and statistical controls, alongside a comprehensive risk analysis of potential failure modes such as misalignment of feedback and low engagement levels.
